{"id":"f607594e-6834-40f7-ba44-22ebf095fa90","object":"chat.completion","created":1790510300,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"parent_requirement_id": "R3", "mode": "residual", "used_claims": ["C2", "C3"], "local_residual": "Establish whether Evita Manji, as Sophie's partner at the time of Sophie's death, gave an interview in which she said that following Sophie's death Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs."}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need parse. We have Original Question complex. Parent Requirement R3: "The partner of the artist (at the time of their death) gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." Supporting claims: C2 Sophie's partner was Evita Manji. C3 In a later online tribute, Sophie's partner Evita Manji said, "She's an immaterial girl now; she can be anything she wants... and she is in everything around us."

We need derive one current local research residual inside fixed parent. Prior alignment partially_supported. Need identify exactly ONE coherent evidence objective inside R3 still needs established. Used claims maybe C2 C3. Need not solve whole. We need output JSON with parent_requirement_id R3, mode residual, used_claims, local_residual.

Parent requirement has conditions:
- artist has partner at time of death
- partner gave an interview
- in that interview said that following death, artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs.

Claims: C2 partner is Evita Manji. C3 later online tribute said quote "She's an immaterial girl now..." This supports partner said something after death, but not necessarily an interview? "online tribute" not interview. And quote "immaterial girl" maybe references song "Immaterial"? But claim doesn't state one of their songs, nor direct reference. Need residual: establish whether Evita Manji gave an interview (not just online tribute) where she said that following Sophie's death, Sophie has become a direct reference to one of her songs. But parent requirement has one coherent objective? Could be exactly that. But maybe we need one facet. Since C3 is not interview and doesn't mention song. Need choose one unresolved part. Candidate: that the statement was made in an interview. Or that the statement identified artist as direct reference to a song. Which is more coherent? We have C3 quote in online tribute, not interview. The parent requirement specifically "gave an interview where they said..." So residual could be "Whether Evita Manji gave an interview (as distinct from an online tribute) in which she made the statement about Sophie becoming a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." That bundles interview + content. But if C3 already supports said something following death, missing content and format. Need maybe local residual: establish that Evita Manji, as Sophie's partner at time of death, gave an interview—not merely an online tribute—where she said Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs. This is exactly parent requirement residual. But instruction: If several independent unresolved parts remain, choose exactly ONE coherent part. Do not bundle independent research objectives. Here "interview" and "said ... direct reference to song" might be two independent unresolved? C3 supports statement following death but not "direct reference to one of their songs" nor interview. Need choose one. Which one? The more essential is content: did partner say artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs? Because C3 has quote "immaterial girl now; she can be anything..." Could be direct reference to song "Immaterial"? But no claim that it was one of their songs? Actually Sophie has a song "Immaterial" from Oil of Every Pearl's Un-Insides. The quote "She's an immaterial girl now" could be a direct reference to the song "Immaterial." But C3 only says quote; no claim identifies it as song reference. The question asks song title one word adjective. "Immaterial" is adjective? Actually immaterial. Need establish that this quote was in an interview? Hmm.

Parent R3: partner gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. The claims support partner and a later online tribute quote. Not interview. Not "direct reference to one of their songs." Which residual is more local? Could be "the occurrence and content of the interview". If we need one coherent evidence objective, we can ask to establish that Evita Manji gave an interview in which she said Sophie had become a direct reference to one of her songs. That's the requirement itself. But if no substantive part supported? C2 and C3 support partner and posthumous statement. The missing piece is the interview and direct reference. We can choose "the interview setting" as one part: Whether Evita Manji's posthumous statement was given in an interview, as opposed to an online tribute. But even if interview, still need content "direct reference to one of their songs." But perhaps C3 quote could be that content if it's in an interview? C3 already has quote but doesn't mention song. So content still missing.

Maybe local residual should be: "Whether Evita Manji stated, in an interview, that following Sophie's death Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs (e.g., rather than only a generic online tribute statement)." This combines but describes exact missing relation. Is that too broad? It is a coherent evidence objective: find the interview statement. The parent requirement is exactly that. Since C2 and C3 partially support, local residual can be the remaining condition. The instruction: "If several independent unresolved parts remain, choose exactly ONE coherent part." But the missing part is a single proposition: the interview statement content. The fact it's an interview and the content are part of same proposition. It might be acceptable.

Could also choose: "Whether the statement Evita Manji made after Sophie's death was an interview statement that identified Sophie as a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." That is coherent.

Need used_claims: C2, C3? We can list those used. Mode residual.

Need no search query. JSON only. Ensure no extra. Use exact schema.

Let's craft local_residual concise, low-commitment. "Establish whether Evita Manji, as Sophie's partner at the time of Sophie's death, gave an interview in which she said that following Sophie's death Sophie has become a direct reference to one of Sophie's songs." This is exactly missing. But maybe "direct reference" maybe phrase from question. Good.

Could mention not just online tribute. This preserves uncertainty. We shouldn't add outside knowledge (e.g., song title). We can say "one of the artist's songs" without naming. Use "Sophie"? Claims use Sophie. Parent says artist. Original question says musical artist. C2 says Sophie. OK.

Need maybe used_claims ["C2","C3"]. Mode residual. parent_requirement_id R3.
